description: We’re not just a team, we’re a close-knit family. Each of us brings something different: creativity, sporty energy, business sense, coding and software skills, and hands-on hardware know-how. Above all, we’re hardworking and never give up. We solve problems together, face challenges side by side, and believe that when diverse talents unite, nothing is out of reach.
summary: Farmers around the world face shifting temperatures, unpredictable rainfall, water shortages and declining soil health, which makes it hard to choose crop rotations that last. BUMI360 proposes a decision-support tool that uses NASA Earth observation data, such as POWER, GPM IMERG, SMAP and MODIS, as a climate and water history for each farm. This data is combined with local soil tests, crop characteristics and farmer priorities to score each rotation option on water fit, climate fit and soil benefit. The result is a ranked list of rotations with clear, easy-to-understand reasons. NASA data has a fairly coarse resolution, and soil health cannot be measured from space, so soil tests are still needed. An early prototype will be built for one region and a few crops to demonstrate the concept.
details:
BUMI360 is an innovative, farmer-centred agricultural decision-support platform that combines NASA Earth observation data, local soil information, and crop science to help farmers make smarter decisions about crop rotation, soil health, and climate adaptation.

The name BUMI360 combines "Bumi", the Malay word for Earth, with "360", representing a comprehensive, data-driven understanding of agricultural conditions.

Our vision is to make satellite-powered agricultural intelligence accessible, practical, and useful for farmers, particularly smallholder farmers in Malaysia.

What does it do?

BUMI360 helps farmers identify which crops to grow, in what sequence, and under which environmental conditions to maintain healthy soils, reduce agricultural risks, and improve long-term productivity.

Traditional crop planning often depends on past farming experience, seasonal expectations, or trial and error. However, climate change is making rainfall, temperature, and water availability increasingly unpredictable.

BUMI360 addresses this challenge through a data-driven crop-rotation recommendation system.

How does it work?

Farmers begin by entering information about their agricultural land, including its location, soil type, soil pH, previously cultivated crops, water availability, and farming objectives. BUMI360 then incorporates relevant NASA datasets to analyse environmental conditions such as rainfall patterns, temperature, soil moisture, vegetation health, and potential drought risks.

This information is evaluated against a database of locally relevant crops, including maize, soybean, peanuts, water spinach, and mustard greens. Each crop has specific environmental requirements, nutrient demands, and compatibility with other crops.

Using a crop-rotation recommendation engine, BUMI360 evaluates possible planting sequences based on climate suitability, soil conditions, nutrient management, crop families, and farmers' preferences.

For example, a farmer who has repeatedly planted maize might receive a recommendation to introduce a legume, such as soybean or peanuts, into the rotation. Legumes can support nitrogen cycling and help diversify the farming system. Bumi360 would check whether those crops are suitable for the farmer's soil, climate, water supply, and farming objectives before recommending them.

The platform aims to present personalised crop-rotation plans, suitability scores, environmental risk indicators, and explanations that help farmers understand why particular crops are recommended.

What benefits does BUMI360 offer?

  • Improved soil health: Encourages crop diversity, better nutrient management, and reduced soil degradation.
  • Greater climate resilience: Helps farmers adapt planting decisions to changing rainfall, temperature, and drought conditions.
  • More efficient resource use: Supports better management of water, fertiliser, and other agricultural inputs.
  • Reduced farming risks: Discourages unsuitable crop combinations and repeated planting of crops vulnerable to similar pests and diseases.
  • Improved economic opportunities: Helps farmers evaluate crops that suit their land while considering market demand and production costs.
  • Accessible agricultural knowledge: Translates complex satellite datasets and agronomic information into understandable recommendations.

Unlike a conventional crop information database, Bumi360 aims to provide location-specific, actionable farming guidance.

What is the intended impact of the project?

Our project aims to improve agricultural sustainability, food security, and climate resilience, currently starting with smallholder farmers in Sarawak, Malaysia.

  • Social impact
    • Empower farmers with understandable scientific information, reduce barriers to agricultural technology, and strengthen local farming communities.
    • Promote healthier soils, crop diversification, efficient water use, and more sustainable agricultural practices.
    • Help farmers make better-informed decisions, potentially reduce avoidable input costs, and improve yield stability over time.
    • Develop a scalable agricultural intelligence platform that could eventually support farmers across Malaysia and other regions facing climate-related agricultural challenges.

BUMI360 also aligns with several United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, including SDG 2 (Zero Hunger), SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production), SDG 13 (Climate Action), and SDG 15 (Life on Land).

These are our intended outcomes. Actual improvements in yields, soil health, or resource efficiency will need to be measured through field testing and farmer feedback.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software were used to develop BUMI360?

BUMI360 is a working web platform, live at bumi360.vercel.app, that combines NASA satellite data, a crop database, an interactive map and modern web tools.

NASA POWER provides 25-year average temperatures for Sarawak. GPM IMERG provides rainfall at about 10 km detail, both monthly normals for 2001–2024 and the rain of the last 60 days. SMAP Level 4 provides this week’s root-zone soil moisture at about 9 km, compared with the usual for the month. This data is downloaded from NASA Earthdata and updated automatically every week by GitHub Actions using Python scripts with NumPy and h5py.

The recommendation engine, written in Python with Flask and hosted on Render, checks soil pH, temperature and seasonal water against each crop’s needs. It also scores the next crop from 0 to 100 using climate fit, crop rotation, soil pH and current rain and soil moisture and works out the exact planting date. Crop data for maize, soybean, peanut, water spinach and mustard greens is stored in an SQLite database, exported to JSON and Excel, and kept in GitHub.

The website is built with TypeScript, React, Next.js and Tailwind CSS, is hosted on Vercel, and works on smartphones, tablets and computers. It includes an interactive Leaflet map of Sarawak’s 12 divisions using OpenStreetMap/CARTO tiles and geoBoundaries boundaries, with colour layers and legends for climate score, expected rain, recent rain and soil moisture.

GitHub is used for source code, version control and automation, testing is done with pytest and Playwright, and development was supported by AI-assisted coding (Claude Code).

No special hardware is needed: farmers only need a phone or computer with a web browser, can use their phone’s GPS to locate their field, and a basic soil pH test is recommended for the most accurate result. Future versions may add MODIS/VIIRS data for vegetation and land temperature, a PostgreSQL/Supabase database for farmer accounts and saved farm histories, Figma for design, and optional soil sensors.

How Is BUMI360 Creative and Innovative?

BUMI360 introduces a practical approach to climate-smart agriculture by connecting satellite technology with the real-world needs of farmers.

Its creativity lies in transforming complex NASA Earth observation datasets into understandable and actionable agricultural recommendations. Rather than presenting raw satellite measurements, the platform interprets environmental information to support decisions about crop selection and rotation.

Unlike conventional crop recommendation systems that primarily focus on identifying individual suitable crops, Bumi360 emphasises long-term crop-rotation planning. It considers how different crops interact across planting cycles, including their nutrient requirements, crop families, soil-health effects, and compatibility with local environmental conditions.

Another innovative feature is its integration of satellite-derived information with farmer-provided soil measurements. This hybrid approach recognises that satellite observations can reveal broader environmental patterns, while local measurements provide important details about individual agricultural fields.

BUMI360 is also designed with Malaysian agriculture in mind. By prioritising locally relevant crops and considering regional growing conditions, the platform aims to provide recommendations that are more practical for farmers in Malaysia, including those in Sarawak.

Furthermore, BUMI360 emphasises transparency and accessibility. Instead of functioning as an unexplained recommendation system, it aims to show farmers the reasoning behind suggested crop rotations, helping them understand the relationship between climate conditions, soil fertility, and crop performance.

By combining Earth observation, soil science, crop-rotation principles, and user-friendly digital technology, Bumi360 seeks to make scientific agricultural decision-making more accessible and practical.

What Factors Did Our Team Consider?

During the conceptualisation and design of BUMI360, our team considered several important factors to ensure that the platform would be scientifically grounded, practical, and accessible to farmers.

Climate variability and environmental risks were major considerations. Increasingly unpredictable rainfall, changing temperatures, drought conditions, excessive precipitation, and extreme weather can significantly influence crop growth and agricultural productivity. Therefore, BUMI360 is designed to incorporate environmental indicators that help farmers assess climate-related risks.

Soil health and fertility were equally important. Soil pH, texture, drainage, nutrient availability, and organic matter influence crop suitability and productivity. The platform considers these factors when evaluating possible planting sequences and recommending practices that support long-term soil sustainability.

Crop characteristics and rotation compatibility were also carefully considered. Different crops have different water requirements, nutrient demands, growing conditions, and biological characteristics. Repeatedly growing crops from the same family can also increase certain pest and disease risks. BUMI360, therefore, aims to recommend crop sequences that promote agricultural diversity and better nutrient management.

Local agricultural conditions were another key consideration. Since the project initially targets Malaysian farmers, the crop database focuses on crops relevant to local farming systems, tropical climates, and regional agricultural practices.

Farmers' economic needs and preferences also influence the platform's design. A crop may be environmentally suitable but impractical if its production costs are too high, its market demand is limited, or the farmer lacks the necessary equipment. BUMI360 therefore aims to balance environmental suitability with practical farming considerations.

Accessibility and affordability were central to the project. Recognizing that some smallholder farmers have limited access to advanced agricultural technology, our team aims to develop a simple, mobile-friendly platform that can operate without expensive hardware. Clear explanations and understandable recommendations are intended to make the system easier to use.

Finally, data accuracy and reliability were important considerations. Satellite observations may have limitations in spatial resolution, measurement uncertainty, and data availability. Furthermore, soil properties can vary considerably within individual farms. To address these limitations, BUMI360 is designed to combine satellite-derived indicators with farmer-provided information and local soil measurements wherever possible.

By considering these environmental, scientific, economic, and technological factors, our team aims to create a solution that is not only innovative but also relevant to the real challenges faced by farmers.

Conclusion

BUMI360 is more than a crop recommendation platform. It represents our vision of using space technology to address challenges on Earth.

By integrating NASA Earth observation data, local soil information, agricultural science, and accessible digital tools, BUMI360 aims to empower farmers to make smarter crop-rotation decisions, protect soil resources, and adapt to changing climate conditions.

Starting with Malaysian agricultural communities, our long-term ambition is to make climate-smart farming guidance more accessible and contribute to sustainable agricultural development.

BUMI360 — Know what your land can grow.
